quote: must be received within 60 days of the initial patient billing
explanation: Your income papers must arrive within 60 days of the first bill. Nothing says you can still apply after that, and California bans time limits on applying.

quote: A report to a consumer credit reporting agency will not be initiated
explanation: This only delays credit reporting until a payment plan fails, so it implies reporting can happen after that. California now bans reporting hospital debt to credit bureaus at any time.

quote: report adverse information to a consumer credit reporting agency or commence civil action against a patient for nonpayment at any time prior to 180 days after the initial billing
explanation: This only bars credit reporting for the first 180 days, which implies it is allowed later. California now bans reporting hospital debt to credit bureaus at any time.

quote: Only one current account statement will be required to verify monetary assets.
explanation: The California policy asks for a bank statement to check your assets when deciding free or discounted care. California law no longer lets hospitals count your savings for this.

quote: may report adverse information to a credit reporting bureau before the extended payment plan has been declared inoperative
explanation: The policy only waits until a payment plan fails, and elsewhere only the first 180 days, before credit reporting. California now bans reporting hospital debt to credit bureaus at any time.
